items.stem: Distinguish between coming together and holding together federations with examples.
items.answer: (1) Coming together: independent states pool sovereignty to form a bigger unit. (2) In coming together federations, constituent states usually have equal power – USA, Switzerland, Australia. (3) Holding together: a large country divides power between centre and states. (4) In holding together federations, the centre tends to be more powerful – India, Spain, Belgium.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for any three points: (1) Coming together: independent states pool sovereignty to form a bigger unit. (2) In coming together federations, constituent states usually have equal power – USA, Switzerland, Australia. (3) Holding together: a large country divides power between centre and states. (4) In holding together federations, the centre tends to be more powerful – India, Spain, Belgium.

items.stem:
(a) Explain how the judiciary helps the working of federalism in India. (3 marks)
(b) Why is it not easy to change the power-sharing arrangement in India? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) Courts interpret the constitution and the powers of different levels. (2) The High Courts and the Supreme Court settle disputes between levels of government. (3) They ensure neither level oversteps its jurisdiction. (4) They protect the federal arrangement from unilateral changes. (b) (1) Changes need the approval of both Houses of Parliament with at least two-thirds majority. (2) They must also be ratified by the legislatures of at least half of the total states.

items.stem:

(b) Why can the fundamental provisions of a federal constitution not be changed by one level of government alone? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) Coming together: independent states pool sovereignty to form a bigger unit. (2) In coming together federations, constituent states usually have equal power – USA, Switzerland, Australia. (3) Holding together: a large country divides power between centre and states. (4) In holding together federations, the centre tends to be more powerful – India, Spain, Belgium. (b) (1) The jurisdictions of each level are specified in the constitution. (2) Such changes require the consent of both levels of government.
